name: Adolf Eichmann
role: SS-Obersturmbannführer; head of RSHA Referat IV B4 (Jewish affairs and deportations), executed 1962
summary: Eichmann was a long-standing National Socialist and SS officer who organised forced Jewish emigration and then the deportation of Jews to the killing sites. He described himself at trial as bound by oath and orders; in the 1957 Sassen interviews, as quoted in published sources, he spoke of the Jews as an enemy and of having no regrets. Only the positions his own record and statements document are recorded here; most statements are left unanswered.

notes: His accounts conflict: at the 1961 trial he said he had no hatred of Jews, never thought annihilation justified and acted on orders, while the 1957 Sassen material (secondhand, via the Jewish Virtual Library and Wikipedia) records him as unrepentant. The trial court found he believed in the Nazi cause. Answers weigh his record of measures he personally drove, and mark contested points low. The interrogation was read into the trial record (see notFound for the prison memoirs and the Less interrogation volume). Themes searched in the later pass: means, world, society and liberty, for the statements added since the first pass; only forced removal of a minority was documented by his record, the rest stay null.
